knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 1.2.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) Distinguish Pearson, Spearman, Kendall. (2) Name one inference caution. (3) Why is 1.2.3 not today's primary?
knowledge_checks.body: Retrieve 1.2.2 closed-book under Publication Front discipline.
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Pearson is linear association; Spearman/Kendall are rank-based. PCA opens tomorrow.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO or claiming Approver clearance / spine / until-exam complete.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 1.2.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Years licensed vs claim frequency: frequency is skewed with visible outliers; the scatter looks roughly decreasing but nonlinear. (1) Which correlation measure would you prefer and why? (2) State one claim a large coefficient still does not justify.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Prefer Spearman (or Kendall) because the relationship looks monotone but nonlinear and outliers can distort Pearson. (2) A large coefficient still does not prove that changing years licensed causes frequency to change.
